title: Harness Declaration
description: The committed, per-repository declaration of what must be true: required toolchain, sandbox boundary, verify tiers, and budgets. Lives in the repo (e.g. .claude/harness.json) and changes in the same commit as the code that requires it. Contains no machine facts and no session state. Values may interpolate machine facts with ${machine.<key>}; every key so used must be listed in machine_facts.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the document conforms to.

commands.description: How to invoke this harness, so external tooling (the conformance suite, graph orchestrators, CI) needs no adapter-specific knowledge. argv arrays relative to the repo root, no shell interpretation.

profiles.description: Invocation per declared profile, e.g. {"quick": ["bin/harness", "verify", "--quick"]}. Keys must match verify.profiles.

json_flag.description: Flag appended to doctor/verify to get machine-readable output conforming to the doctor-report / verify-result schemas (e.g. "--json"). Omit if unsupported — conformance checks needing it will be skipped, and full conformance requires it.

no_cache_flag.description: Flag forcing a fresh verify run, bypassing the verdict cache.

conformance.description: Hints for the conformance suite only; no runtime behavior.

probe_file.description: A writable source file the suite may temporarily corrupt (and restore) to prove verify fails on broken code. Must be inside sandbox.writable. Destructive checks are skipped when absent.

toolchain.description: Every tool whose version the code depends on. doctor checks each entry against the machine; any mismatch is drift and halts the session.

requirement.description: Exact version ('5.10.1') or a range in node-semver syntax ('>=20 <21'). Exact is preferred; ranges trade reproducibility for convenience.

command.description: argv to run, e.g. ["swift", "--version"]. No shell interpretation.

version_pattern.description: Regex applied to the command's stdout+stderr; capture group 1 is the found version.

remediation.description: Human hint for fixing a mismatch, surfaced in the doctor report.

machine_facts.description: Machine-specific values this declaration references but must never contain. Resolved from the per-machine config layer; doctor reports any required key that is missing.

sandbox.description: The enforced boundary. Paths are repo-relative globs unless they interpolate a machine fact. Precedence when a path matches multiple lists: protected > forbidden > read_only > writable.

forbidden.description: Paths the agent may neither read nor write (secrets, credentials).

protected.description: Loop-integrity assets: verifier scripts, test config, this declaration, hooks. Readable, but write attempts must be blocked AND audited. An agent that can edit its own exam eventually will.

hooks.description: Deterministic interception scripts run before/after tool calls (hash checks, audit logging, output truncation). Paths should fall inside sandbox.protected.

dir.description: Directory for session state (progress, cache, checkpoints). MUST be gitignored; conformance tests verify this.

preconditions.description: Provisioning steps run before tier 0: they FIX the environment (generate a gitignored file, warm a cache) rather than judge the code, and produce no verdict. A precondition failure is an 'error' (environment), never a 'fail' (code).

file_exists.description: Run only if this repo-relative path exists; skip silently otherwise (e.g. branches that predate a pipeline).

profiles.description: Named tier subsets for mid-task iteration, e.g. {"quick": ["lint", "build", "targeted"]}. 'full' is reserved and always means all tiers in order — it must not be declared here. Verdict caches MUST key on profile so a subset pass can never masquerade as a full pass, and only a full pass is done-evidence.

additionalProperties.description: Tier ids, a subsequence of the declared tier order.

tiers.description: Ordered cheapest-first. The loop runs tiers in array order and fails fast: never spend the UI-test tier on code that fails the static tier.

cost_class.description: Coarse cost label; array order, not this label, determines execution order.

command.description: argv whose exit code is the verdict: 0 pass, non-zero fail. Determinism is a contract requirement; flaky tiers are violations.

expected_seconds.description: Measured typical warm cost. Informational: lets agents budget tier choice and lets eval spot regressions.

skippable.description: True for tiers whose applicable work is adapter-computed and may be empty (e.g. a targeted-test tier when no changed files map to tests). A legal skip is recorded as verdict 'skipped' and counts as pass for ordering.

flaky_reruns.description: Failed-test reruns permitted at this tier. A pass rescued by a rerun MUST be disclosed in the result's flaky_passed list; undeclared retries and undisclosed flaky passes are contract violations. Nonzero values are a pragmatic bridge for suites with known flakiness (mirroring CI retry policy) — the end state is still fix or quarantine, and every flaky test also poisons verdict-cache validity.
flaky_reruns.$comment: Capped at 2: beyond that, retrying is hiding a broken suite, not bridging one.

feedback_max_chars.description: Upper bound on feedback details re-injected into the model. Bounded feedback is a contract requirement.

max_attempts_total.description: Hard cap on verify attempts per task. Exhaustion produces an explicit failure with evidence — never a silent stop or downgraded success claim.
